provenance.generatedBy: claude-opus-5-5 · Field Kit v2 Prompt A batch
provenance.notes: Ext family batch. Licensed trade and the most agency-pitched vertical, so copy leans on local proof and storm-chaser contrast. No shingle or financing brands. Ranges are planning figures, not quotes.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Roof age, soft decking, granules in the gutters, curling or lifted shingles, leaks at flashing and pipe boots, and when a patch is honest advice
pageStructurePlus.why: Most roofing calls start with 'can I get away with a repair'. A straight answer before the visit is what earns the inspection.

pageStructurePlus.contains: What the free roof inspection covers, a sample report with marked shots of flashing, vents, valleys and decking, and how long the visit takes
pageStructurePlus.why: Showing the report up front turns a free inspection from a sales visit into a service the homeowner can trust before a ladder goes up.

pageStructurePlus.section: Roof tear-off day, step by step
pageStructurePlus.contains: Dumpster placement, tarps over shrubs, driveway protection, magnetic nail sweep, noise and start times, pets, and the final walk with the crew lead
pageStructurePlus.why: The worry after signing is a crew on the house for a day. Explaining tear-off day removes the last reason to delay the start date.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Architectural shingle, standing-seam metal and tile compared by lifespan and look, colour samples on common house styles, and HOA colour approval notes
pageStructurePlus.why: Once the roof is approved, couples decide colour together on a phone at night. A picker keeps that decision on your site, not a supplier's.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Intake and exhaust venting, ridge vents, attic heat, ice dams at the eaves, bath fans venting into the attic, and what a vent fix costs to add
pageStructurePlus.why: Ventilation explains why the last roof failed early, and it justifies a line item a cheaper roofer leaves off the quote.

pageStructurePlus.contains: Emergency tarp request, what to photograph before anyone climbs, how to spot a storm chaser at the door, and the local office address
pageStructurePlus.why: After hail or wind, homeowners pick the roofer who is clearly local and answers first. This page says both before the trucks from out of state arrive.

designDirections.name: Ladder Up
designDirections.bestFor: One- and two-crew roofers who win on a fast inspection and a phone that gets answered after a storm
designDirections.headlineSample: Roof repair and replacement in {City}, inspected first
designDirections.whyItFits: Steel blue and a plain grotesque read like an estimate sheet. Everything points at the inspection request and the tap-to-call bar.

designDirections.name: Ridge to Gutter
designDirections.bestFor: Established roofing companies with a deep file of tear-offs, new roofs and storm repairs to show street by street
designDirections.headlineSample: New roofs and storm repairs, done right in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: The family's own combo. Evergreen and a refined serif feel like an insurer, which is the calm a worried homeowner wants, and the before-after hero shows the old roof and the new one.

designDirections.name: Slate and Copper
designDirections.bestFor: Slate, tile, cedar shake and standing-seam metal roofers selling to older and larger homes
designDirections.headlineSample: Slate, tile and metal roofs built to outlast the house in {City}
designDirections.whyItFits: A private-bank palette and old-style serif suit a roof bought once in a lifetime, where the buyer is choosing a craftsman, not a price.

openers.line: Your Google listing has Call and Directions but no website, so a homeowner with a leak over the kitchen can't check that you're a real local roofer before they dial.
openers.hook: Open their Maps listing and confirm there is no Website button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Here's what would sit behind that button for a roofer: {demo-link}

openers.line: The website link on your listing opens your Facebook page. Someone comparing three roof replacement quotes wants your warranty and an inspection form, not a feed.
openers.hook: Tap their Website link and confirm it lands on Facebook. Note the newest roof they posted there.
openers.linkLine: A page built for the roof buyer, not the feed: {demo-link}

openers.line: The site on your listing still shows a free-host banner. A roof is a once-a-generation purchase, and people want to see that the roofer will be around for the warranty call.
openers.hook: Open the site and look for a builder banner, an old copyright year or a dead contact form. Note which one you found.
openers.linkLine: Same roofing company, current and quick on a phone: {demo-link}

openers.line: I opened your roofing site on my phone and the call button sat under the menu. Most people searching for a roofer are standing in the yard looking up at the damage.
openers.hook: Only if they have a site. Load it on your phone and note exactly what breaks: menu, gallery or call button. Screenshot it for when they reply.
openers.linkLine: Your roofing site rebuilt for a phone in the driveway: {demo-link}

openers.line: There's no way to ask you for a roof inspection except calling. A lot of homeowners notice the stain on the ceiling at night and would rather send the address and a description than leave a voicemail.
openers.hook: Check the listing, the social pages and any site for a form. If there is none, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: An inspection request that asks for roof age and the leak spot: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your drone shots of finished roofs are sharp, the clean ridgelines especially. Right now they're scattered between job-site memes instead of sitting in a roofing gallery a buyer can scroll.
openers.hook: Find two finished roofs on their grid you could describe by material and colour. Mention one if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those finished roofs, sorted by material: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your Google reviews mention crews that picked up every nail and a roof that stopped a leak two other roofers missed. Nobody reads that unless they're already on your listing.
openers.hook: Read their reviews and copy one specific phrase about a roof job or the cleanup. Quote it back if they reply.
openers.linkLine: Those roof reviews next to the jobs they describe: {demo-link}

openers.line: Once hail season starts, out-of-state storm crews flood {City} with door hangers. The local roofer with a real site and an office address is the one people trust.
openers.hook: Use this in late winter or early spring, before the first big hail or wind event. Name the season in the reply.
openers.linkLine: Ready before the first storm hits: {demo-link}

openers.line: Roof leaks show up during the storm, usually at night. When the call to a roofer goes to voicemail, that homeowner tries the next number until somebody promises a tarp.
openers.hook: Call their listed number after hours. If it goes to a full or generic voicemail, the angle holds.
openers.linkLine: A leak and tarp request that works at night: {demo-link}

openers.line: Saw you're hiring roofers and a crew lead. Good installers check whether a roofing company looks established before they climb for it, same as customers do.
openers.hook: Only if they posted a hiring story, a help-wanted note or a sign on the trailer. Note the date of the post.
openers.linkLine: A roofing company page with a careers section: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your listing says you roof {City} and the towns around it, but there's no page telling a homeowner in {Neighborhood} you'll come out. That town plus 'roofer' is what they type.
openers.hook: Find the towns they mention in posts or reviews. Use the one furthest from their shop.
openers.linkLine: A roofing page for each town you cover: {demo-link}

openers.line: If you offer payment plans on roof replacements, that belongs on a page. A full tear-off is the kind of number people want to see split up before they invite a roofer over.
openers.hook: Only if they mention financing somewhere: a post, a review, the truck wrap. If they don't, skip this angle.
openers.linkLine: Roof financing explained before the inspection: {demo-link}

openers.line: Your roofing licence is on the state registry, but a homeowner never sees it. Showing the licence, the insurance and any manufacturer certification is the first thing that separates you from a storm chaser.
openers.hook: Look them up on the state contractor registry. Note that a record exists; never quote a number you didn't see.
openers.linkLine: Licence, insurance and warranty on one roofing page: {demo-link}

openers.line: Sounds like most of your roofs come from neighbours who watched a tear-off on their street. That works until the street is done, and even a referral searches your roofing company before calling.
openers.hook: Look for review text like 'neighbour recommended' or 'did our whole street'. Quote it back.
openers.linkLine: Where a neighbour's roofing referral would land: {demo-link}

openers.line: That {specific recent job} you posted is a clean roof, straight lines and tidy flashing. A job like that should be the first thing a stranger sees, not three scrolls down a feed.
openers.hook: Pick the newest finished roof on their grid and name it exactly: material, colour, and the street if they tagged it.
openers.linkLine: That roof job, front and centre: {demo-link}

sequence.dm1:
Hey {Owner}, that {specific recent job} you posted is a clean roof, tidy flashing and a straight ridge.

I searched for roofers in {City} and found {Business Name} on social but no site with your licence, warranty and an inspection request. I put together a sample roofing page to see how it would look, with marked placeholders where your photos would go.

Want me to send it over?
sequence.dm2:
{Owner}, following up in case my last message got buried under storm calls. Here's the sample roofing site for {Business Name}: {demo-link}

It has an inspection request that asks for roof age and where the leak is, a repair-or-replace guide, and a page that shows your licence and insurance before a stranger knocks. If it's not for you, say so and I'll leave you be.
sequence.call:
"Hi, is this {Owner}? I'm {Your Name}, I build websites for roofing companies here in {City}. I sent you a message a couple of days ago, did it come through?"

IF NO:
"Easy to miss in roofing season. Short version: I built a sample roofing site for {Business Name}, with an inspection request, a repair-or-replace guide and your licence up front, and marked placeholders where your photos would go. Can I email you the link to look at tonight?"

IF YES:
"What did you think?"
 → let them talk, don't fill the silence
"I know you get pitched by marketing agencies every week. This isn't leads or ads, it's a site you own. The build runs {Build Range} depending on how many town and material pages you want, then {Care Range} a month for hosting and changes. For a roofer your size I'd quote about {Build Price}, which is a small slice of one replacement."
"Can I walk you through it for ten minutes, Tuesday or Thursday evening?"

CLOSE:
"I'll send a one-page scope and a deposit invoice. We start the day it clears, and it's live before the next storm."

objections.objection: Agencies call me every week. You're just another one.
objections.handler: "Fair. The difference is I built the roofing site first instead of asking for a meeting. No ad budget, no lead contract. You own the domain and the site either way."

objections.objection: I get all my roofs from referrals and insurance adjusters.
objections.handler: "Then your roofs sell themselves. A referral still searches your name before calling, and an adjuster's homeowner wants to see you're licensed. The site is where both land."

objections.objection: I already pay for shared roofing leads.
objections.handler: "Shared leads go to several roofers at once and you pay whether you win the roof or not. Your own site sends that homeowner to one roofer, you."

objections.objection: Storm season is when I'm too busy to think about this.
objections.handler: "That's why I'm calling now. The site gets built while it's calm, so it's answering inspection requests when you're on a roof all day."
"Good, that's cheaper than me. Happy to hand over the inspection form and the repair-or-replace guide. If it stalls before storm season, the offer stands."

objections.objection: Roofing is all about price. People take the low bid.
objections.handler: "Some do. The site is for the ones comparing what's in the bid: tear-off versus layover, ventilation, flashing, the warranty. That's what makes your number make sense."
"{Build Range}. For you it'd be about {Build Price}, because it's an inspection form, a gallery and a few town pages. That's less than the materials on one small roof."

email.subject: Roofing site for {Business Name}

sequence.voicemail: "{Owner}, it's {Your Name}. I build websites for roofing companies in {City}, and I put together a sample one for {Business Name}, inspection form and all. I'll email the link. Have a look when you're off the roof. {Your Phone}. Thanks."
sequence.takedown:
{Owner}, I'm taking the {Business Name} roofing demo down on Friday to free up the space.

Want me to leave it up? One word is fine either way.
sequence.nurture:
Hey {Owner}, hail and wind season is a few weeks out and the inspection calls are about to start. Thought of you.

The roofing site is still here whenever you want it, same price as before. {demo-link} if you want another look.

bullets: Peg the build to a sliver of one roof replacement, never to an hourly rate. Roofers think in squares and jobs.
Price the inspection request as its own line when it asks for roof age, leak location and upload of ceiling stains.
Material pages (shingle, metal, tile, flat) are separate lines; each answers a different search and a different buyer.
Only quote storm-response pages for roofers who actually do tarps and emergency calls.
Town pages scale with the service area; quote them per town, and only for towns where they have finished roofs.
Expect a long close. Roofers have heard every agency pitch, so lead with the finished demo and a short scope, not a package.

lineItems.description: Max when the page has a lifespan comparison, colour samples and its own gallery of finished roofs in that material.

lineItems.item: Inspection request with leak and roof-age fields
lineItems.description: Max with photo upload, storm-date field, insurance-claim question and routing to two estimators.

lineItems.item: Storm tarp and leak landing page
lineItems.description: Max with an urgent request form, a switch-on storm banner and a storm-chaser warning checklist.
Max when each town page gets its own finished roofs, local permit notes and a review from that town.

lineItems.item: Roof colour picker on house styles
lineItems.description: Max when it covers several house styles, shingle and metal colours, and a save-and-share link for the spouse.

lineItems.item: Tear-off day and ventilation explainer pages
lineItems.description: Max with a printable prep checklist and simple attic venting diagrams drawn for their roofs.
Max when the inspection form, the repair-or-replace guide and the warranty page are all translated.

whatElseYouSell.name: Drone roof photo day
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "One morning flying your three best new roofs gives you top-down shots of every ridge and valley, a full gallery and a year of posts."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, or the week they finish a roof they're proud of.

whatElseYouSell.name: Google profile posts for every finished roof
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every new roof goes on your Google profile with the town and the material in the caption, so the map listing shows recent tear-offs, not last year's."
whatElseYouSell.when: Day 30, once the site is live and a new roof is finished.

whatElseYouSell.name: Review requests after each tear-off
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "The day the dumpster leaves, the homeowner gets a text asking how the roofing crew did. Those reviews are what a storm-season searcher reads first."

whatElseYouSell.name: Local Services Ads setup with the licence badge
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Roofing is licence-checked on those ads, so the badge does the trust work. I set it up, handle the disputes on junk leads and keep the roofing categories tight."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once reviews are flowing and their licence and insurance documents are current.

whatElseYouSell.name: Yard sign, trailer and dumpster banner artwork
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "A tear-off is the loudest advert on the street for two days. A yard sign and a dumpster banner with the site on them make the whole block remember the roofer."

whatElseYouSell.name: Neighbour door hangers around each roof job
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When a roof goes on, the houses either side get a door hanger with the finished job and a free inspection offer. Their roofs are the same age."
whatElseYouSell.when: Month 2, once there are finished roofs on the site to point at.

whatElseYouSell.name: Post-storm neighbourhood campaign
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "When hail hits a part of {City}, a storm page, a map post and a mailer to those streets go live that week, all pointing at a local roofer with a real address."
whatElseYouSell.when: Build in the off-season, switch on the week a storm is reported.

whatElseYouSell.name: Annual roof check-up mailer
whatElseYouSell.pitchLine: "Every past roofing customer gets a spring postcard offering a check of flashing, boots and gutters. It keeps you top of mind for the warranty and the neighbours."
whatElseYouSell.when: Pitch in late winter, mail in early spring.

withoutAI.route: Gutter crews who follow the new roof
withoutAI.whoPays: The gutter company, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Who hangs the gutters after your roofing crew leaves? I'll build their site too, and your roof page links to theirs."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Roof and gutter jobs run back to back and the owners already refer each other. One introduction is a warm door.

withoutAI.pitchLine: "Your roofing supply branch sells to every roofer in the region and their site is a catalogue. Introduce me and I'll build their contractor finder."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Supply branches have real budgets, and their contractor list is the prospect list you would otherwise build by hand.

withoutAI.route: Home inspectors who flag aging roofs
withoutAI.pitchLine: "Every inspection report that flags a worn roof sends a buyer looking for a roofer. The inspectors you know need sites as much as you did."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors and roofers swap referrals constantly, and the inspector buys a site on the same logic: look established, get booked.

withoutAI.route: Public adjusters on roof damage claims
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The adjusters who work your storm claims need a site that explains what they do in plain words. You know them already."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Adjusters live on trust and referrals from roofers. A roofer's introduction gets you past the first call.

withoutAI.whoPays: The insulation contractor, at your normal rate
withoutAI.pitchLine: "When your roofing crew finds a hot attic, someone blows in insulation after. That contractor needs a site, and your ventilation page links to them."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Attic work is the natural next job after a roof. Both sides gain a referral partner.

withoutAI.route: Small landlords with roofs to maintain
withoutAI.pitchLine: "The landlords whose rental roofs you patch need a simple tenant request page. I build it, and roof leaks route to your roofing crew."
withoutAI.whyItWorks: Landlords with a dozen doors have a real maintenance problem and a vendor they already trust.

withAI.route: Order assistant for the roofing supply branch
withAI.pitchLine: "Give every roofer on the branch's books a tool that turns roof measurements into a shingle, underlayment and flashing order, priced from that branch."
withAI.whyItWorks: It ties roofers to one branch's pricing, which is worth more to the branch than a rebate.

withAI.route: Claim photo organiser for public adjusters
withAI.pitchLine: "Adjusters drown in roof damage photos from each storm. An assistant sorts them by slope and damage type and drafts the photo log."
withAI.whyItWorks: Storm weeks are when adjusters have no time. A tool that saves them hours sells itself on the first storm.

withAI.route: Plain-language report summaries for home inspectors
withAI.pitchLine: "Buyers don't read a long inspection report. An assistant turns it into a one-page summary, with roof and attic findings first."
withAI.whyItWorks: Inspectors compete on how clear their reports are. The roofer's introduction makes the first demo easy.

withAI.route: Estimate follow-up for the gutter company
withAI.pitchLine: "The gutter crew that follows your roofs loses estimates to slow callbacks. The same follow-up texts you run, set up for them in a week."
withAI.whyItWorks: You built it once for the roofer. The second build is configuration, and the referral came from someone they trust.

withAI.pitchLine: "An assistant checks each re-roof request against the HOA's approved shingle colours and materials before the board sees it."
withAI.whyItWorks: Boards meet rarely and a rejected colour delays a roof by a month. Managers pay to end the back-and-forth.

withAI.pitchLine: "Tenants report 'water in the ceiling' at midnight. An assistant asks the right questions, marks the roof leaks as urgent and sends them to one roofer."
withAI.whyItWorks: Managers save dispatch time and the roofing client gets steady repair work from people who already pay on time.

softwareAI.name: Missed-call text-back for roof leak calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every call you miss while you're on a roof gets a text asking for the address and whether it's leaking now. You call back knowing which one is urgent."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Day 30. Needs their business number forwarded and two lines of wording they approve.

softwareAI.name: Roof replacement price estimator by squares
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner picks the house size, the pitch and the roofing material and sees a ballpark range before the inspection. You stop driving out to people shopping for the cheapest layover."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their real price per square by material, tear-off and decking adders, and the smallest roof they take.

softwareAI.name: Inspection report builder with marked photos
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Snap the flashing, the boots and the soft spots on the roof, tap what's wrong, and a clean branded report goes to the homeowner before you leave the driveway."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their inspection checklist, a logo and two past reports they liked.

softwareAI.name: Review reply drafts that name the roof job
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Each new review gets a reply drafted in your voice that mentions the roof, the street and the cleanup, ready to approve from the truck."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2, alongside review requests. Needs ten of their past replies to learn the voice. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Deposit and material-drop invoicing
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Deposit at signing, the next draw when the shingles land on the driveway, the balance at the final walk, each sent automatically with a card link."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 2. Needs their draw schedule and the payment account they already use.

softwareAI.name: Aerial roof measurement estimator
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Type an address and it drafts the roof's squares, pitch and ridge length from aerial views, so the estimate is half done before you climb."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4, after the price estimator. Needs a set of past roofs with measured squares to check against. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: After-hours storm line for leak calls
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers at two in the morning during the storm, asks where the water is coming in, books the tarp visit and texts you only if it's urgent."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, ahead of storm season. Needs their calendar, the tarp price and the questions they always ask. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Roofing job board from inspection to final walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every roof inspection, signed contract, permit, material delivery and install date on one board instead of a whiteboard in the shop."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3, once the inspection form is producing. Needs their stages, who sells, and how permits are pulled.

softwareAI.name: Roof warranty registry with transfer letters
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Every roof you install goes on a registry with its warranty dates, and when the house sells, a transfer letter goes to the new owner with your number on it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a list of past roofs with install dates and their written workmanship terms.

softwareAI.name: Insurance supplement draft assistant
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Compare the adjuster's roof scope with your inspection and it drafts the missed items, drip edge, starter and vents, for you to check and send."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5, for roofers who work claims. Needs a few past scopes and supplements. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; you always review before sending.

softwareAI.name: Material order and delivery scheduler
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When a roof is booked, the shingle and underlayment order and the dumpster drop get scheduled for the right morning, and the homeowner gets a heads-up text."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 3. Needs their supply branch contact, dumpster vendor and booking flow.

softwareAI.name: Customer portal with colour sign-off and start date
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The homeowner signs off on the shingle colour, sees the permit status and the tear-off date, and stops calling the office to ask."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs the job board in place first.

softwareAI.name: Hail-swath alert to past roofing customers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When hail is reported over a part of {City}, every past roofing customer in those ZIP codes gets a text offering a free check. You reach them before the door knockers do."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs a customer list with addresses and a storm report feed for their area.

softwareAI.name: Chatbot on roof types, warranties and lead times
softwareAI.pitchLine: "It answers 'metal or shingle for my house' and 'how soon can you start' at midnight, from your real roofing notes and schedule, and takes a number when it doesn't know."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 4. Needs their material notes, warranty terms and current lead time, updated monthly. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Voice-to-estimate notes from the roof walk
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Walk the roof, talk into the phone about layers, decking and vents, and it drafts the roofing estimate on your template."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 5. Needs their estimate template and pricing rules. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

softwareAI.name: Hail and wind damage pre-screen from homeowner uploads
softwareAI.pitchLine: "A homeowner uploads shots of the roof and gutters after a storm, and the tool flags likely hail or wind damage so you send the inspector to the real ones first."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs a library of past storm inspections with notes. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer; it never tells a homeowner a claim will pay.

softwareAI.name: Crew app with tear-off and flashing checklist
softwareAI.pitchLine: "The crew lead checks off decking, ice and water shield, flashing and the nail sweep on a phone, with a shot at each step. You see every roof without climbing it."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, when they run two crews. Needs their install checklist and a crew lead willing to test it.

softwareAI.name: Job costing by roof squares and crew
softwareAI.pitchLine: "See which roofs actually made money once shingles, dumpsters, decking replacement and crew days are counted."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6. Needs material invoices and crew days for a season of roofs.

softwareAI.name: Supply branch price-sheet sync
softwareAI.pitchLine: "When the supply branch changes shingle or underlayment prices, the roof estimator and the estimate template update the same day."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Month 6, after the estimator. Needs the branch's price sheet format.

softwareAI.name: Applicant screener for roofers and helpers
softwareAI.pitchLine: "Applicants for roofer and ground-crew jobs answer your questions about heights, harness training and a ride to the job, and you only call the ones who fit."
softwareAI.whenAndWhatItTakes: Any time they post a hiring note. Needs their must-haves and the pay range. Comes with the AI maintenance retainer.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Productise the inspection report builder for roofers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I built this roof inspection report for one roofer. Every roofing company in the state hands homeowners a messy report."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: The hard part of vertical software is knowing the workflow. The first roofer taught it to you and paid for the build.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Contractor finder licensed to a roofing distributor
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Put a find-a-roofer map on your site for every roofing contractor who buys from your branches. They stay loyal to the branch that sends them work."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Distributors already spend on contractor loyalty. A tool roofers use daily is stickier than a rebate.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Certified-roofer portal for a shingle or metal maker
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your certified roofers need warranty registration, spec sheets and a locator. I've built that workflow for a roofer already."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Manufacturers have channel budgets and a dealer problem. The roofing client is your proof that you know the trade.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Offer every member roofer a site template with an inspection form and a storm-chaser warning page as a membership benefit."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Associations need reasons to renew, and fighting storm chasers is already on their agenda.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Roofing site template for marketing agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Your agency signs roofers and builds each one from scratch. License my roofing template with the inspection request and tear-off pages already done."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agencies own the roofing relationship; you sell them the part you've already finished.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Each roofing territory needs its own town pages and an inspection form that routes to the right owner. I build it once and roll it out."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: One contract becomes many territories on the same template.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Storm page kit for roofers in hail states
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A switch-on storm page, tarp request and hail alert text, ready for any roofer in a hail belt the week weather hits."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Every hail-state roofer needs it the same week. Selling it as a kit means no custom build for each.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Approved-roofer page for independent insurance agencies
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "After a storm, policyholders ask their agent which roofer to call. A vetted local roofer page on the agency's site answers it."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Agents want to look helpful to clients after a loss, and the roofing client becomes the first name on that page.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "A short monthly sheet on where shingle, metal and underlayment prices are heading, built from the supply price lists roofers share with you."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roofers re-price jobs constantly. Built only from data they contribute, it never claims more than the sheets show.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: Continuing-education pages for roofing licence trainers
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "Where roofing licences need renewal hours, the trainers need class pages and sign-ups. Your roofer client knows which ones are any good."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Trainers sell to every licensed roofer in the state, and a roofer's referral is the introduction.

routesToBiggerBuyer.route: One roofer per metro, next city over
routesToBiggerBuyer.whoPays: A roofing company in a new metro
routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "I build for one roofing company per city. {City} is taken; the next metro's best local roofer isn't."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Exclusive geography is a selling point to roofers, and the template, pitch and demo carry straight over.

routesToBiggerBuyer.pitchLine: "An agency started your roofing site and stopped answering. I can finish it on a template already live for another roofer."
routesToBiggerBuyer.whyItWorks: Roofing is the most agency-pitched trade, so there are plenty of half-built sites. Those owners already decided to buy.

upsellLadder.offer: Roofing site build plus care plan, one contract
upsellLadder.trigger: They say yes to the demo.
upsellLadder.line: "The roofing site and the care plan go on one contract, so a storm banner or a new phone number is a text to me, not a weekend for you."

upsellLadder.trigger: The first roof finished since launch, with a happy homeowner on the driveway.
upsellLadder.line: "That roof you finished Tuesday deserves a review while the dumpster's still fresh in their mind. Let's ask every roofing customer the same day."

upsellLadder.trigger: The roofing gallery still has marked placeholders, or they post a roof they're proud of.
upsellLadder.line: "Let's fly your three best roofs in one morning. The gallery fills and you have top-down shots for a year."

upsellLadder.offer: Inspection report builder with marked photos
upsellLadder.trigger: Sixty days of inspection requests, and they mention writing reports at night.
upsellLadder.line: "You're writing roof reports after dinner. This builds them on the roof and sends them before you leave."

upsellLadder.offer: After-hours storm line for leak calls
upsellLadder.trigger: A storm passes and the missed-call log shows leak calls overnight.
upsellLadder.line: "Those leak calls during the last storm went to whoever answered. This answers them and books the tarp."

upsellLadder.offer: Local Services Ads setup with the licence badge
upsellLadder.trigger: They pass a steady count of new reviews and their licence and insurance documents are current.
upsellLadder.line: "Your reviews are strong enough now for the licence-checked roofing ads. Let's put the badge in front of the next storm's searches."

upsellLadder.offer: Roofing job board from inspection to final walk
upsellLadder.trigger: They mention a second roofing crew or a backlog of several weeks.
upsellLadder.line: "Two roofing crews and a backlog won't fit on the shop whiteboard. Let's put every roof on one board."

upsellLadder.offer: Roof warranty registry with transfer letters
upsellLadder.trigger: A past roofing customer sells their house, or the first install anniversary passes.
upsellLadder.line: "When a house you roofed sells, the new owner should get your warranty letter, not a stranger's door hanger."
